pages.lesson:
LESSON: WEALTH, MONEY AND POVERTY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Christian Living Today
Topic 5.4: Wealth, Money and Poverty

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Wealth, Money and Poverty. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Which vices are associated with love for money?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money, and poverty

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Wealth, Money and Poverty.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Wealth, Money and Poverty using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Team up to read, discuss and make notes based on the following scriptures; Deuteronomy 8:18, Ecclesiastes 5:10-19, Proverbs 15:27, and Matthew 6:24-27,
2. Use the internet or the library to search for information on causes of poverty today and the remedies; make a presentation using a chart or a digital device,
3. Interview a resource person on how to make money using credible ways as a youth and note key points,
4. Imagination and Creativity: the skill of reflection is demonstrated as learners implement a business idea, assess its success, and improve it based on the feedback they get.
5. Digital Literacy: the skill of appropriately selecting digital technology relevant to different tasks is exhibited as learners undertake different tasks and make presentations. Values:

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which vices are associated with love for money?
2. Why is integrity important in handling money and wealth?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Wealth, Money and Poverty is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
